cards.question: A footballer wins a tournament’s Golden Boot. What did they lead the tournament in?
cards.answerExplanation: The Golden Boot recognizes the top goalscorer. Assists can decide a tiebreak in some competitions, but they are not the main criterion; clean sheets belong to goalkeeper awards. It spotlights finishing rather than all-around play.
cards.whyNow: Cameroon’s women have just celebrated a landmark continental title, including individual tournament honors that make football’s best-known awards timely.

cards.question: A cargo spacecraft carries food and fuel to a station but no passengers. What mission is it doing?
cards.answerExplanation: An uncrewed resupply mission delivers cargo for people already in orbit. A crew rotation mission transports astronauts or cosmonauts; spacewalk and repair missions have entirely different purposes.
cards.whyNow: NASA is preparing coverage of a Progress spacecraft that will bring several tons of supplies to the International Space Station.

cards.question: For the U.S. jobless rate, someone without work is generally counted as unemployed only if they are doing what?
choices: Actively seeking and available to work
cards.canonicalAnswer: Actively seeking and available to work
cards.answerExplanation: The official measure generally counts people who have no job, actively looked for work recently, and are available to take one. Receiving benefits is not required, and working part-time means a person is employed, not unemployed.
cards.whyNow: The latest U.S. employment report has put payrolls and unemployment figures at the center of economic news.

cards.question: Which part of the UK is not part of Great Britain?
cards.answerExplanation: Great Britain is England, Scotland and Wales. The UK includes those three plus Northern Ireland, which is on the island of Ireland. The distinction matters in travel, maps, sport and official statistics.
cards.whyNow: A September 4 update on child-facing work applies across several UK nations, making this common map distinction timely.

cards.question: Which EU country keeps its own visa and border rules rather than joining Schengen?
cards.answerExplanation: Ireland has an opt-out from Schengen and keeps its own visa and border policies. Austria, Spain and Sweden are in Schengen, where internal border checks have generally been abolished.
cards.whyNow: A September 4 visa debate turns on the often-confused boundary between the EU and the Schengen travel area.
